transitions.use: proposed far-infrared (about 35 micrometre) transition 4f9 6s2 6H°15/2 - 4f8 5d 6s2 8G13/2 with enhanced sensitivity to variation of the fine-structure constant (theory proposal: enhancement factor about -140); no measurement

use_source.source: Karshenboim, Nevsky, Angstmann, Dzuba, Flambaum, "A New Option for a Search for alpha Variation: Narrow Transitions with Enhanced Sensitivity", arXiv:physics/0511180 (2005)

conflicts: No two opened sources give the same quantity for Tb I, so no numerical conflict could be checked. Note: Malcheva et al. 2013 state in their abstract that time-resolved laser-induced-fluorescence lifetimes of Tb I are systematically shorter than the older delayed-coincidence values (numbers not accessible).
not_found: Lifetimes of every drawn excited level (19131.45, 23043.43, 23107.25, 23147.92, 25076.26, 25717.68, 25825.53, 26087.13, 26385.99, 27102.94 cm^-1): measurements exist (Malcheva, Engström, Lundberg, Nilsson, Hartman, Blagoev, Phys. Scr. 88, 045304 (2013): 7 odd + 11 even levels; Feng et al., J. Phys. B 43, 225001 (2010): 27 odd levels at 27220-33293 cm^-1, 6.5-43.9 ns) but both are paywalled / captcha-blocked; only abstracts read, no numbers available. No Wisconsin (Den Hartog/Lawler) Tb I data set exists as far as could be found (their Tb work is on Tb II).
Transition probabilities / branching fractions of Tb I lines: none found (NIST lists no A values for Tb I either).

Hyperfine constants of the ground level 4f9 6s2 6H°15/2, of 6H°13/2 (2771.675) and of 8D11/2 (2310.09): measured by Childs, Phys. Rev. A 2, 316 (1970) (17 lowest levels, atomic-beam magnetic resonance) - paywalled, only the abstract was read (it gives Q(159Tb) = +1.34(11) b but no A, B).

Hyperfine constants of the drawn excited levels: measured by the Poznan group (Furmann, Stefanska et al.: Spectrochim. Acta B 2015; J. Phys. B 49, 025001 (2015); J. Phys. B (2017), doi:10.1088/1361-6455/aa8370; JQSRT 2019, 2023, 2024-25) and by Wang et al., J. Anal. At. Spectrom. (2024, Fourier-transform spectra, A for 45 Tb I levels) - all paywalled or access-blocked.

Laser cooling: a feasibility study exists (Search for the laser-cooling schemes in the terbium atom, J. Quant. Spectrosc. Radiat. Transfer 2025, doi:10.1016/j.jqsrt.2025.109375) but could not be opened; no experimental cooling of Tb found.
Precise transition frequencies and measured level energies beyond NIST: none found.
notes: 159Tb is the only stable isotope (I = 3/2), so there are no isotope shifts between stable isotopes. Very thin file: nearly all Tb I atomic data sit behind paywalls or bot protection (IOP, Elsevier, APS, RSC). The four hyperfine entries were read from the publisher abstract pages of the Optica journals, whose HTML embeds the tables, through an automated page reader (both tables were read twice with identical results). The 8G hyperfine constants are 1966 optical-interferometry values converted from mK and marked derived. Level 509.845 (8G11/2) and 4670.455 (6H°11/2) are not drawn by the site but carry the only precise data. Extra fields beyond SCHEMA.md: top-level ionization_limit; transition field use_source.
